fit: oral corn oil comparator and unstimulated salivary flow
assessment: The six-month Sjögren trial reports no clear change in unstimulated whole sialometry or group difference in dryness. The study evaluates autoimmune hyposalivation and does not measure Parkinson drooling or report oil grade.

fit: topical oxidized corn oil derivative and dry-mouth symptoms
assessment: The randomized 24-person crossover used a topical active comparator derived from oxidized corn oil. Baseline hyposalivation and treatment-period symptom ratings do not estimate dietary corn oil or Parkinson drooling.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and measured walking and trotting stride
assessment: Randomized horse comparison recorded similar walking stride changes. The omega-3 arm had a larger descriptive trot-stride change, between-arm p=.08. Animal, diet and gait differences limit clinical transfer.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and 400-m walking speed
assessment: Fish oil versus matched corn-oil gelcaps gave +0.010 m/s, 95% CI −0.025 to +0.044. Usual walking speed in mobility-impaired older adults does not estimate Parkinson stride length.

fit: corn oil plus maltodextrin comparator and 4-m gait speed
assessment: The corn-oil regimen had +0.12 m/s within-arm gait speed change with a rehabilitation co-intervention. The small pilot did not estimate stride length or an isolated oil effect.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and arm-specific serious fall reporting
assessment: Registry counts are 1/71 for corn-oil-only placebo and 1/109 for fish-oil-only active treatment. The pooled journal fall row includes different placebos. Routine fall frequency and a Parkinson population are unavailable.

fit: oral corn oil comparator and VAS fatigue
assessment: A six-month Sjögren trial reports no clear group difference in fatigue or 24-hour sleep/rest time when comparing corn oil and evening-primrose gamma-linolenic acid. The public abstract omits grade and arm-level fatigue estimates.

fit: corn oil feed and measured canine odor thresholds
assessment: Behavioral olfactometry tested corn, coconut and beef-tallow diets with conditioning strata. The reported deterioration concerned unconditioned dogs on coconut oil. Trial results do not establish corn-induced worsening.

fit: maize oil addition and canine odor detection crossover
assessment: Maize oil diet improved adjusted near-threshold detection against a distinct high-fat diet. Comparisons with the original low-fat maintenance diet and tests of absolute odor thresholds showed no clear differences. Refining and Parkinson disease were unmeasured.
